authority_limit: ABAC guidance does not select SAN attribute authorities, policies, combining rules, acceptable assurance, business effects or legal mandates.
bounded_implication: Authorization evaluates subject, object/resource, requested operation and environment attributes against policy, rules or relationships; authentication is a distinct concern.
title: NIST SP 800-162: Guide to Attribute Based Access Control

authority_limit: A XACML decision is not authentication, entitlement issuance, enforcement, effect completion, business acceptance or universal policy validity.
bounded_implication: Authorization decisions distinguish Permit, Deny, Indeterminate and NotApplicable, with explicit policy combining, obligations/advice, PDP and PEP seams.
title: XACML Version 3.0 Core Specification

authority_limit: The profile does not establish real-world mandate, identity, unlimited transitive delegation, enforcement or acceptance.
bounded_implication: Administrative authority and policy issuance can be delegated under scoped constraints and issuer chains.
title: XACML 3.0 Administration and Delegation Profile

authority_limit: Policy expression does not prove legal validity, identity, effective authority, duty discharge, enforcement or effect completion.
bounded_implication: Permissions, prohibitions, duties, consequences, remedies, constraints, offers and agreements have distinct normative positions and conflict strategies.
title: ODRL Information Model 2.2

authority_limit: OAuth token issuance does not establish user identity, domain entitlement semantics, resource-owner mandate, safe use or business acceptance.
bounded_implication: Resource owner, client, authorization server and resource server roles exchange scoped authorization grants and access tokens.
title: RFC 6749: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework

authority_limit: Revocation is not deletion, recall of prior disclosure, proof that caches have converged or reversal of completed effects.
bounded_implication: A token can be invalidated through a revocation endpoint, with implications for related tokens and propagation.
title: RFC 7009: OAuth 2.0 Token Revocation

authority_limit: An active token is not proof of subject identity, request appropriateness, business authority, policy freshness at every cache or completed enforcement.
bounded_implication: A protected resource can query authorization-server state and metadata about a presented token, including whether it is currently active.
title: RFC 7662: OAuth 2.0 Token Introspection

authority_limit: Verification does not prove claim truth, holder-subject identity, issuer authority for every purpose, current acceptance or authorization.
bounded_implication: Issuer, holder, verifier, credential subject, claims, validity, status and evidence are distinct; securing a credential protects it from undetected tampering.
title: Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0

authority_limit: Attestation integrity or a verifier result is not universal trust, application authorization, semantic fitness or absence of defects.
bounded_implication: Attester, Verifier and Relying Party roles separate evidence production, evidence appraisal, attestation results and application-specific relying decisions.
title: RFC 9334: RATS Architecture

authority_limit: Identity assurance does not itself grant domain authorization, approve an action, establish purpose or accept an effect.
bounded_implication: Identity proofing, authentication and federation use separate assurance models, authenticators, assertions and relying-party decisions.
title: NIST SP 800-63-4 Digital Identity Guidelines

authority_limit: SLSA verification does not prove source correctness, runtime safety, semantic fitness, authorization or production acceptance.
bounded_implication: Supply-chain provenance and attestations carry scoped claims with verification expectations and threat-model limits.
title: SLSA Specification v1.2

authority_limit: Authenticity and integrity of an attestation do not establish predicate truth, issuer mandate, completeness or relying-party acceptance.
bounded_implication: Attestations bind predicates and subjects in signed statements whose consumers apply policy to scoped claims.
title: in-toto Attestation Framework
